key_sub: Convert nm to m and eV to J (× 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹).
body_html:
How to think about it

Light comes in photons of energy E = hf = hc/λ. In the photoelectric effect one photon frees one electron: hf = φ + Ek(max). Below the threshold frequency no electrons are emitted, however bright the light.

Electrons also behave as waves: λ = h/(mv). Hadrons are made of quarks (baryons qqq, mesons q q̄); leptons are not. Charge, baryon number and lepton number are always conserved.

Example

Find the energy of a 500 nm photon in eV.

E = hc/λ = 3.98 × 10−19 J

÷ 1.60 × 10−19

Answer: 2.49 eV

Example

A metal has φ = 2.3 eV. Photons of 3.1 eV hit it. Find Ek(max).

3.1 − 2.3

Answer: 0.8 eV

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to change nm into m (× 10⁻⁹).
  • Thinking brighter light gives faster photoelectrons.
  • Mixing up baryons (three quarks) and mesons (quark and antiquark).

faq.a: hf = φ + Ek(max): the photon energy equals the work function plus the maximum kinetic energy of the electron.

faq.q: What is the de Broglie wavelength?
faq.a: λ = h/(mv). Moving particles such as electrons have a wavelength, shown by electron diffraction.
